desc: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. It is 446 km long, up to 29 km wide, and attains depths of over 1,800 meters. The canyon exposes nearly 2 billion years of Earth's geological history through its colorful rock layers. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most famous natural landmarks in the world. The canyon was formed over 5-6 million years of erosion by the Colorado River. It is home to diverse ecosystems from desert scrub to conifer forests across its elevation gradient. The Grand Canyon National Park receives over 5 million visitors annually.
fact: The Grand Canyon is 446 km long, 29 km wide, and 1,800 meters deep · It exposes nearly 2 billion years of geological history in its rock layers · It was carved by the Colorado River over 5-6 million years · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site attracting over 5 million annual visitors

desc: Fjaðrárgljúfur is a spectacular canyon in southeast Iceland, carved by the Fjaðrá River through 2 million-year-old palagonite rock formations. The canyon is up to 100 meters deep and about 2 km long, with dramatic winding walls covered in lush green moss. It was formed during the Ice Age when glacial meltwater carved through the volcanic bedrock. The canyon gained international fame as a filming location for the TV series Game of Thrones. The walls reveal layered volcanic ash and lava from ancient eruptions beneath a glacier. The canyon is protected as a natural monument with restricted access to preserve its fragile ecosystem.
fact: Fjaðrárgljúfur is a 100-meter deep canyon in Iceland carved through volcanic palagonite rock · It was formed by glacial meltwater during the Ice Age · It was a filming location for Game of Thrones · The canyon walls show layered volcanic ash from ancient subglacial eruptions

desc: Kali Gandaki Gorge is the deepest gorge in the world, located in Nepal between the Himalayan peaks Annapurna I (8,091 m) and Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m). The gorge is carved by the Kali Gandaki River with a valley floor at about 2,520 meters, giving a relative depth of nearly 5,600 meters. The gorge is older than the mountains surrounding it, a phenomenon known as 'river antecedence' where the river maintained its course as the Himalayas rose. The gorge is an important trade route between Tibet and India and contains sedimentary rocks with abundant marine fossils, evidence that the region was once under the Tethys Ocean.
fact: The Kali Gandaki Gorge is the deepest gorge in the world at nearly 5,600 meters relative depth · It lies between Annapurna I (8,091 m) and Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m) in Nepal · The gorge is older than the surrounding Himalayas, demonstrating river antecedence · It is an ancient trade route between Tibet and India with abundant marine fossils

desc: Tiger Leaping Gorge is a deep canyon on the Jinsha River, a tributary of the Yangtze River, in southwestern China's Yunnan province. It is one of the deepest gorges in the world, with a maximum depth of about 3,790 meters where the river runs between the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain (5,596 m) and the Haba Snow Mountain (5,396 m). The gorge is divided into three sections: Upper, Middle, and Lower Tiger Leaping Gorge. It is named after a legendary tiger that leaped across the narrowest point. The gorge is a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas. It is a popular destination for trekking and white-water rafting.
fact: Tiger Leaping Gorge is one of the deepest gorges in the world at 3,790 meters depth · It runs between Jade Dragon Snow Mountain and Haba Snow Mountain in Yunnan, China · It is named after a legendary tiger that leaped across the narrowest point · It is part of the UNESCO Three Parallel Rivers World Heritage Site

desc: Cotahuasi Canyon is one of the deepest canyons in the world, located in the Arequipa region of southern Peru. It reaches a depth of 3,535 meters, carved by the Cotahuasi River through the Andean plateau. The canyon is deeper than the more famous Colca Canyon and second only to the Kali Gandaki Gorge in measured depth. The canyon walls expose volcanic and sedimentary rock layers spanning millions of years. The area is home to the Andean condor, vicuña, and ancient terraced agriculture systems built by the Wari and Inca civilizations. The canyon's remote location preserves traditional Quechua-speaking communities and their pre-Columbian farming practices.
fact: Cotahuasi Canyon is one of the deepest canyons in the world at 3,535 meters depth · It is located in the Arequipa region of Peru · It is home to the Andean condor and vicuña · The canyon preserves traditional Quechua communities with pre-Columbian terraced agriculture
